cues.en: When
cues.zh: 什么时候

cues.en: do you want to die? The reaper is busy, but he can fit you in right now. Too soon, later perhaps,
cues.zh: 你想死？死神很忙，但他现在就能安排你。太早了，或许以后，

cues.en: future you will keep the appointment,
cues.zh: 未来的你会赴这个约，

cues.en: old and with a life fully lived, perhaps ever so slightly bored and ready. Now you might think that, but when the appointment whippersnapper you set comes, it is not in the future because you don't live in the future. You always live in the now, and thus, you always die now.
cues.zh: 年老，度过完整的一生，也许有点厌倦了，也准备好了。现在你可能会这么想，但当你设下的那个预约到来时，它并不在未来，因为你不活在未来。你永远活在现在，因此，你永远死在现在。

cues.en: Because the reaper comes for all eventually, humans have formed a relationship with death perverse. Like a hostage who grows to love their kidnapper, humans tell themselves the handful of decades the reaper gives them is just the right length. That living a truly long and healthy life would get boring and would be unnatural.
cues.zh: 因为死神终会找上所有人，人类与死亡形成了一种扭曲的关系。就像人质渐渐爱上绑架者，人类告诉自己，死神给的那几十年长度刚刚好。真正长寿健康的生活会变得无聊，也不自然。

cues.en: And imagine all the problems if death took a holiday. And so the reaper of age whispers that he is your friend. Always near. Growing humans bigger, stronger, healthier, and smarter
cues.zh: 再想象一下，如果死亡放个假，会有多少问题。于是衰老的收割者低语说，他是你的朋友。始终靠近。让人长得更大、更强壮、更健康、更聪明

cues.en: at first. Then comes his harvest of slow rot. Death is a part of life, he whispers. Death gives life meaning. This is madness.
cues.zh: 起初如此。然后是他缓慢腐坏的收割。死亡是生命的一部分，他低语道。死亡赋予生命意义。这简直是疯狂。

cues.en: Misery doesn't give happiness meaning. Happiness is meaning itself. If you tortured people to make them better appreciate the pleasures of life, you would be a monster, just like this guy. No parent would ask the reaper of age to wrinkle their child's skin, weaken their bones, dim their vision and their minds, cripple them in a thousand ways over decades to ultimately kill them, to give their life meaning. But what can you do? The world contains pain and death, and so your brain believes the sweet lies that the horrors you can't avoid
cues.zh: 痛苦并不赋予幸福意义。幸福本身就是意义。如果你折磨别人，让他们更懂得欣赏生命的快乐，你就是个怪物，就像这家伙一样。没有父母会请求衰老的收割者让孩子的皮肤起皱、骨骼变弱、视力和心智衰退，在几十年里以千百种方式让他们残弱，最终杀死他们，只为赋予他们生命意义。但你能怎么办呢？世界包含痛苦和死亡，于是你的大脑相信了甜蜜的谎言：你无法避免的恐怖

cues.en: are good for you. And while death is a part of life,
cues.zh: 对你有好处。而且，虽然死亡是生命的一部分，

cues.en: cholera was a part of life until humans developed wells and sewers to separate water from waste. Short sightedness is a part of life until it isn't. Just because a thing is natural doesn't make it good or necessary.
cues.zh: 霍乱曾是生命的一部分，直到人类发明水井和下水道，把水与污物分开。近视也是生命的一部分，直到不再是。事物是自然的，并不意味着它就好或必要。

cues.en: It's natural to live lives nasty,
cues.zh: 人活一世，往往痛苦、

cues.en: brutish, and short. And it's natural for humans to look at what indifferent nature provides as the starting point, as a to do list. Where humans focus, technology ever improves.
cues.zh: 野蛮而短暂。人类自然会把这冷漠大自然所给予的一切当作起点，当作待办清单。人类关注哪里，技术就在哪里不断进步。

cues.en: And with that, the ability to make lives better ever improves.
cues.zh: 随之而来的是，让生活变得更好的能力也在不断提高。

cues.en: And just now, some basic tools with real promise to slow or halt the decay are becoming visible on the horizon. Which raises the question, just how strong is the reaper of age? With enough time and attention, can humans craft these basic tools into shields and swords to keep him at bay?
cues.zh: 而就在现在，一些真正有望减缓或阻止衰老的基石工具，已经隐约出现在地平线上。这就引发了一个问题：岁月这个死神究竟有多强大？只要有足够的时间和关注，人类能否将这些基础工具打造为盾牌和长剑，将他拒之门外？

cues.en: Possibly indefinitely?
cues.zh: 甚至可能是无限期地？

cues.en: Perhaps.
cues.zh: 也许吧。

cues.en: And if so, the first immortal generation
cues.zh: 如果是这样，那么第一代长生不老的人

cues.en: may be alive
cues.zh: 可能

cues.en: today.
cues.zh: 今天就已经活在世上了。

cues.en: A generation that lives a healthy adulthood as long as they wish to. But to make that happen, brains need to be cleared of the millennia of death acceptance.
cues.zh: 这一代人将拥有他们所希望的那样漫长而健康的成年期。但要实现这一点，人类的大脑必须洗去数千年以来对死亡的逆来顺受。

cues.en: Death is not a solution to future problems imagined.
cues.zh: 死亡并不是解决未来虚构问题的办法。

cues.en: Faced with the changes longer lives will bring, humans will not miss the reaper and construct one to solve their problems. Just as with our larger cities, we don't remix the water to bring back cholera.
cues.zh: 面对更长的寿命将带来的巨变，人类不会怀念死神，也不会为了解决问题再去创造一个死神。就像在我们的大型城市里，我们不会把水重新弄脏来让霍乱卷土重来。

cues.en: Humans must discard the learned helplessness the reaper and their own brains have imposed on them. To instead see the rot and decay not as natural and inevitable, but as a degenerative disease to be attacked like all the others. As the degenerative
cues.zh: 人类必须摒弃死神和自身大脑强加给他们的习得性无助。不再将衰老和腐朽视为自然且不可避免的现象，而是将其视为一种退行性疾病，像攻克其他所有疾病一样去攻击它。将其视为一种

cues.en: disease that affects one hundred percent of the population
cues.zh: 会影响百分之百人口的

cues.en: and is a source of misery untold.
cues.zh: 退行性疾病，以及无数痛苦的根源。

cues.en: Misery not in your distant future,
cues.zh: 痛苦不在遥远的未来，

cues.en: but in your now.
cues.zh: 而就在当下。

cues.en: And how soon we start the project of focusing our attention and shaping our tools against the reaper matters. For the difference of but a day might determine
cues.zh: 我们何时开始聚焦注意力、打造工具来对抗这位死神至关重要。因为哪怕只差一天，都可能决定

cues.en: what side of the future chasm you find yourself on. Journeying forever forward or falling backward
cues.zh: 你会发现自己站在未来鸿沟的哪一边。是一路向前，还是向后跌落

cues.en: into the abyss.
cues.zh: 深渊。

cues.en: Is it too late for you? We probably won't win the war against death because death is all powerful, but we might be able to win the battle against the next best thing, aging itself.
cues.zh: 对你来说已经太晚了吗？我们大概无法赢得对抗死亡的战争，因为死亡拥有无上的力量，但我们或许能赢得对抗其次灾难的战斗，也就是衰老本身。

cues.en: There's a realistic chance that you might live a longer and healthier life, but should we really do it? We explore this in our video.
cues.zh: 我们确实有切实的机会过上更长寿、更健康的生活，但我们真的应该这么做吗？我们将在视频中探讨这个问题。
